text:
emma: running into a 403 when switching projects in the console using a delegated token after rotating an API key. user sees console UI but actions are blocked. repro steps below. any quick ideas?

mike: can you paste the exact curl and response body? also which project id + account?

emma: repro steps: 1) rotate api key in acct: acme-corp (org: acme) 2) exchange for delegated token with scope 'project:read project:write' 3) hit console /api/v1/projects/switch with header Authorization: Bearer <delegated-token> 4) UI flashes then shows 403 "permission denied".

emma: curl I used:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/switch \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci..." \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"project_id":"proj-acme-prod"}'
```

emma: response:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "message": "missing scope: project:impersonate or project:admin",
  "code": 403
}
```

luis: aha — the message hints the delegated token doesn't include impersonation scope. when rotating API keys we sometimes drop the delegated scope mapping. are you using an OIDC exchange or our api-key->delegated flow?

emma: api-key -> delegated flow via our internal exchange service (token-exchange svc). this used to include project:impersonate implicitly. after rotation it only has project:read project:write.

mike: that's consistent. quick workaround: reissue delegated token with impersonation scope or temporarily grant user project admin then switch. but let's not grant admin if we can avoid.

raj: tagging eng-auth for a root fix. @luis can you capture logs for token-exchange at 1746789100-1746789300 window? we need to see scope mapping logic change.

luis: on it. pulled logs and found this line in token-exchange v2: 
```
2025-07-12T14:45:07Z INFO exchange: mapped scopes [project:read project:write] from api_key:ak_123 -> delegated token; implicit_impersonate=false
```

luis: config diff shows a recent default change that toggled implicit_impersonate to false for rotated keys. looks like a safety change that didn't migrate older rotation flows.

emma: ugh. customer is in PROD and hitting blocked UI now. they reported right after we rotated the key automatically per commit-based rotation policy.

mike: escalate. create a support ticket and request a privileged delegated token for their session while we patch. small risk window.

support-bot: Ticket SUP-2026-73 created. Priority: P1. Assigned to: raj. ETA initial response: 30m.

raj: I've opened an internal incident and added eng-auth + infra. short-term fix: luis can generate a one-off delegated token with project:impersonate for their user id (uid: u-8743). emma — can you confirm the user's display id and whether the client is using ephemeral sessions?

emma: user id is u-8743, client is long-lived web session (not ephemeral). please also whitelist the project switch route for the session so UI unblocks.

luis: generated token and provided to support contact via secure channel. instructed customer to retry. they confirmed success — console project switch succeeded after using the new token. :thumbsup:

raj: next steps: 1) patch token-exchange default for rotated keys to preserve implicit_impersonate for service->delegated flows where api-key had that mapping, 2) backfill a migration to re-enable implicit_impersonate for recent rotations in the last 24h, 3) add a regression test for rotation->delegated scope preservation.

mike: also notify compliance for the temporary token issuance and log the justification.

emma: customer satisfied for now. keep me posted on patch timeline.

raj: assigning followups to eng-auth. I'll update SUP-2026-73 and post status here when patch rolls.

support-bot: SUP-2026-73 status updated -> investigating.

luis: patch PR opened: github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/4821 — change is small, hopeful hotfix today.

emma: thanks everyone. going to close the immediate loop with customer. please ping when it's deployed.

raj: will do.
